title: Regional queue-pressure capacity worksheet — July 2026
summary: Working worksheet capturing a set of small-batch autoscaling experiments that use a derived 'queue pressure' signal (requests_in_queue + tokens_in_flight normalized by GPU_capacity) to drive min/max adjustments and scale triggers. Goal: reduce P99 tail latency and scale oscillation while preserving cost. This doc records experiment configs, raw snapshots, qualitative observations, and recommended follow-ups.
raw_metrics_snapshot: snapshot_time=2026-07-19T23:00:00Z; region=us-west-2; avg_gpu_util=62%; avg_queue_len=18.6; tokens_in_flight=84k; measured_queue_pressure=0.58; observed_scale_events_last_24h=14; p50=24ms; p95=110ms; p99=210ms; cost_estimate_last_24h=$3,880
observations: 1) Queue-pressure (requests + tokens normalized by capacity) correlates with P99 spikes more reliably than raw GPU_util or queue_len alone, especially for short-burst workloads. 2) Introducing a soft_window (sustained pressure over N seconds) reduced flip-flop scale events by ~40%. 3) Longer hysteresis combined with soft-window delays slower scale-ups for sustained surges but avoided thrash on noisy workloads. 4) lead_lag_probe (active probe that measures delta in p95/p99 after a temporary small-scale change) provided a useful signal to trigger cooldowns in regions with high variance. 5) Backpressure_ratio (blocked_requests / total_requests) helps catch head-of-queue congestion in reranking pipelines where token-in-flight underestimates load.
recommendation: Adopt queue_pressure as primary up-trigger in mixed and short-burst regions (us-west-2, ap-southeast-1) with a soft_window of 300s and hysteresis 180–300s; keep conservative max caps for p99-sensitive models. For large long-running model profiles (large-rerank) add backpressure_ratio as a secondary up-trigger. Deploy lead_lag_probe as an optional diagnostic in eu-central-1 to refine cooldown thresholds. Update autoscaler to expose 'soft_window' and 'backpressure_ratio' toggles in the control plane and add a dashboard panel for queue_pressure time-series and probe outcomes.

notes_and_qualifiers: This worksheet mixes live cluster snapshots and testbed experiments. Cost deltas are rough estimates (reserved capacity amortization not included). Some experiments ran with slightly tweaked batch/kv-cache settings — see linked PR for exact test harness configs. Keep conservative during initial rollout; model teams with strict latency SLOs should opt into per-model overrides rather than global aggressive scaling.
appendix_examples: example_formula_queue_pressure = (requests_in_queue + tokens_in_flight / average_tokens_per_gpu) / (gpus_allocated * gpu_capacity_factor); example_backpressure_ratio = blocked_requests / total_requests; soft_window = duration_seconds where metric must exceed threshold before scaling action. Example probe schedule: probe_size=1% traffic, probe_duration=30s, measure p95_delta over 60s after probe
